cleanIntro: Colt publishes NO disassembly for the Model D revolvers — the Detective Special included. The instruction is one sentence long: do not strip your revolver. What follows is the clearing, the one thing that does open, and the cleaning Colt does publish.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger
steps.action: Before anything else, point the revolver in a safe direction and keep your finger off the trigger. Colt heads its own unloading procedure with that instruction rather than assuming it.
steps.prose: A Model D has no manual safety and no cylinder latch you can feel through a holster. Muzzle discipline is the safety.
steps.quote: NEVER TAKE ANYONE'S WORD THAT A GUN IS UNLOADED: check for yourself with fingers off the trigger and gun pointed in a safe direction, so that you never fire the gun accidentally when you think it is unloaded.
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — SECTION 3 SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, caution 3, p.8
steps.warn: ENSURE THAT THE REVOLVER ts NOT LOADED BEFORE CLEANING, SO THAT IT WILL NOT FIRE.

steps.title: Open the cylinder
steps.action: Pull the cylinder latch to the rear and push the cylinder out to the left of the revolver.
steps.prose: Latch back, cylinder out. This is the only part of a Model D that opens, and it is the entirety of what the manual calls opening the revolver.
steps.quote: pulling cylinder latch to the rear and pushing the cylinder out to the left of revolver
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 2, p.24

steps.title: Push the ejector rod and take the rounds out
steps.action: Push the ejector rod backwards to force out all live rounds or empty cases, remove them from the revolver once they are clear of the chambers, and let the ejector rod return forward under its spring action.
steps.prose: One firm push clears all six. If a case drags, push again rather than picking at it with the cylinder half out.
steps.caution: IF YOU ARE UNLOADING LIVE AMMUNITION, BE CAREFUL NOT TO LET IT FALL ONTO A HARD OBJECT OR SURFACE, AS IT MAY FIRE.
steps.quote: Push ejector rod backwards forcing out
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 3, p.24

steps.title: Look at every chamber
steps.action: Look into every chamber and make sure all of them are empty before cleaning begins.
steps.prose: Colt's wording is EVERY chamber and ALL are empty, in capitals. On a swing-out cylinder that check takes two seconds and there is no excuse for skipping it.
steps.quote: Look EVERY chamber and make sure ALL are empty.
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — SECTION 5 MAINTENANCE, p.32

steps.title: Close it back up when the rounds are out
steps.action: With the hammer not cocked, push the cylinder back into the frame until the cylinder latch springs forward and locks it, then collect the ammunition for safe storage.
steps.prose: Never close a Colt cylinder by flicking the wrist. Push it in and let the latch do its own work.
steps.quote: Push cylinder into the frame until cylinder latch springs forward to lock cylinder.
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 4, p.25

steps.title: Colt publishes no strip for this revolver
steps.action: Do not strip your revolver. That is the manufacturer's whole instruction on the subject: the Model D manual contains no disassembly procedure of any kind, and directs any additional maintenance to Servicing and Repair.
steps.prose: This is a prohibition on one operation, not a statement that the gun cannot be cleaned. Everything the manual does publish — bore, chambers, frame, exterior — is done with the cylinder swung out and the revolver otherwise whole.
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — SECTION 5 MAINTENANCE — IMPORTANT, p.32
steps.warn: If additional maintenance is required, Colt directs you to Servicing and Repair rather than to a screwdriver.

steps.title: Check this manual covers your revolver
steps.action: This book is Colt's Model D manual. Its ammunition table lists Agent, Cobra, Commando Special, Detective Special, Diamondback, Police Positive and Viper, and Colt states the manual applies to all of them — and to commemorative issues of the same types.
steps.prose: Aluminium-frame and steel-frame Model Ds take different ammunition: the table limits +P .38 Special use on the aluminium guns. Check which frame you have against that table, not against the model name alone.
steps.caution: It also applies to commemorative issues of the same type.
steps.quote: Different types of Model D revolvers are shown in the following table, and this safety and instruction manual applies to all of them.
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — SECTION 2 MAIN FEATURES, p.5

steps.title: Cylinder open is the whole of it — now clean it while it is fresh
steps.action: Cylinder swung out, ejector rod free, chambers verified. That is the extent of what opens on a Detective Special, and the extent of what Colt asks you to open. Go straight into cleaning: the manual asks for it as soon after firing as possible.
steps.prose: The Model D lockwork sits behind a side plate that this manual never mentions removing. Its absence from the book is the answer, not an omission.
steps.quote: You should clean your revolver as soon after firing as possible so that the job will be easier
steps.cite: Colt Model D Revolvers Safety and Instruction Manual — Detective Special, Commando Special, Diamondback, Police Positive, Agent, Cobra, Viper — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — SECTION 5 MAINTENANCE — WHEN TO CLEAN, p.32

deepAbsentReason: Colt publishes no disassembly at all for the Model D revolvers. The manual's maintenance section carries one line on the subject — "Do not strip your revolver. If additional maintenance is required see 'Servicing and Repair' later in this instruction manual" (p.32) — and every cleaning instruction in the book is written for a revolver that is whole with the cylinder swung out. So this listing has NO deep clean, and no field strip either: that is the manufacturer's answer, not a gap in ours.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Open the cylinder first, then attach a cotton flannel patch to the cleaning rod, insert it at the muzzle and pass rod and patch down through the barrel; repeat, changing patches, until the last comes out clean
Avoid contact between the cleaning rod and the muzzle — resultant wear reduces accuracy
Take care not to strike the rear frame of the revolver: Colt warns that burring the metal around the firing pin hole can contribute to firing failures

cleaning.name: CYLINDER AND CHAMBERS
tasks: Clean each of the six chambers with the same method used on the barrel

If barrel or chambers remain dirty after firing, use a brass wire bristle brush dipped in gun cleaning solution and pass it all the way through before reversing direction — changing direction with the brush inside will jam it
Note that painted and plated surfaces can be damaged or streaked by gun cleaning solution; follow the solution maker's instructions
Clean the front face of the cylinder — that is where the burn ring builds

cleaning.name: FRAME AND EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the rear face of the barrel, the revolver frame and the front face of the cylinder with a small toothbrush, then remove all trace of gun cleaning solution

Lightly moisten a flannel patch with gun oil and pass it once through the barrel and similarly oil the six chambers; pass a dry patch through instead if the revolver is going back into use rather than storage
Check no flannel or brush bristles have lodged anywhere in the revolver, then wipe all external surfaces — including between hammer and frame — with a lightly oiled flannel patch
Remove any gun cleaning solution and oil from the grip

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Clean as soon after firing as possible — the job is easier and there is less opportunity for corrosion to start
Unfired, clean it once or twice a year in a temperate climate, or as often as once a month in a tropical one
If you carry it loaded, unload it and clean it at least once a month
Below freezing, avoid oil and apply a dry lubricant sparingly instead

reassembly: There is nothing to reassemble: the revolver was never taken apart.
With the hammer not cocked, push the cylinder back into the frame until the cylinder latch springs forward and locks it.
Do not flick the cylinder closed — push it in and let the latch seat itself.
Store the revolver unloaded, with ammunition kept separately and both locked away.
fncheck: With every chamber checked empty and the cylinder closed, cock the hammer through a full rotation and confirm the cylinder indexes and locks on each chamber, then repeat double-action. Check the cylinder latch holds the cylinder firmly closed and that the ejector rod returns fully forward under its own spring.
